\section{Setting and protocol}
\textbf{Task and data.} We forecast the congestion class (free flow, slowed, congested) of a road segment 15, 30, 60 and 120 minutes ahead, from the measured speeds of the Traffic4cast benchmark ~\cite{neun2023t4c} in Madrid, London and Melbourne (828, 774 and 587 segments). The classes come from a congestion factor relative to free flow. The series are one-week blocks separated by gaps; only origins whose input window and targets keep the 15-minute cadence are used. The forecast is scored by weighted cross-entropy (wCE): the cross-entropy of the predicted class probabilities, with class weights that give the rare congested class the same total weight as the others.

\textbf{The inductive regime.} The segments of a city are split into instrumented (observed), validation-hidden and test-hidden sets, each made of whole blocks of a grid, so that a hidden segment is not surrounded by observed ones by construction. A hidden segment never enters the model: not as input, not as a training target, not in the normalisation or in the class weights. The model must forecast a segment it has never seen, from its instrumented neighbours and from the calendar alone.

\textbf{The reference.} G0 is Graph WaveNet ~\cite{wu2019gwnet} with its graph removed: the same temporal network, with no spatial exchange. G1 is the same model with the road graph. In this regime the forecast is close to the uniform predictor: on the pilot configuration (Madrid, a compact sub-network of 95 nodes), the best validation wCE of G0 and G1 was 1.066–1.071, about 3\% below ln 3 = 1.099.

\textbf{A positive control.} The pipeline is not what limits the forecast. When the hidden nodes of the same configuration enter the loss as training targets, never as input, the same model reaches 0.94 with a monotone learning curve, against 1.07 when they are truly unseen. Propagation gains reported for hidden segments that are training targets measure that condition, not an installation.

\textbf{Scales of reading.} V is the difference in wCE from G0, in points of the G0 wCE (percent), positive when the compared arm is better. Intervals are 95\%, from a joint resample of seeds and blocks of the network. Each pre-registration reads two scales: the sign of the interval, and a margin of 3 points. A statement is ``undetermined'' when the pre-registered condition can be neither met nor excluded everywhere. All experiments were run on one machine (Mac M3 Max) and signed before any test metric was computed.
